# speech

The local speech service the harness runs for its clients: the whisper.cpp and Kokoro pipeline as the harness server's child, its state and endpoints, and transcription and synthesis over ACP so a phone needs no speech model.

- **Runs in:** the harness process
- **Source:** [lisp/modules/harness-speech.el](../../lisp/modules/harness-speech.el)
- **Loaded:** when enabled (see `harness-enable-modules`)
- **Requires:** [stacks](stacks.md)

## About

Speech to text and text to speech are services, not capabilities of
a keyboard: whisper.cpp and Kokoro are large, they want a machine
with a CPU to spare, and a phone has neither the room for the models
nor a place to run them.  So the local voice pipeline is the harness
server's, not a client's, and every client shares the one pipeline
over the network, as docs/computers.md says a program that offers an
API other processes share runs next to the server.

This module owns it.  The harness process starts the pipeline and
stops it; a client asks for its state and for speech, never for a
program to run on itself:

  `harness-speech-local-stt-command`  a program the harness runs for
  `harness-speech-local-tts-command`  speech to text and text to
                                      speech, serving at the URL
                                      beside it (`...-stt-url`,
                                      `...-tts-url`); they are child
                                      processes of the harness and
                                      end with it.

With no commands the bundled `voice-local` compose stack runs
instead -- whisper.cpp and Kokoro in containers, published on
loopback only -- and the URLs are the ones the runtime gave it.

Clients reach the pipeline over ACP:

  `speech/status`      what runs, where, with which voice and model,
                       and the one line a client shows when it
                       cannot be used
  `speech/start`       start it; the answer is the state as it is
  `speech/stop`        stop it
  `speech/transcribe`  {audio: BASE64 WAV} -> (:text TEXT)
  `speech/synthesize`  {text: TEXT} -> (:audio BASE64 WAV)

The last two are the sharing: a client sends its audio on the
connection it already has, the harness posts it to the service on
its own loopback, and the answer comes back the same way.  Nothing
is published to the network for that, and a phone needs no
whisper.cpp.  A client on this machine may use the URLs
`speech/status` reports instead, which is what the Emacs live voice
sidecar does.  `speech/changed` carries the state whenever it moves.

## Provides

### Methods

- `speech/start` — Start the local pipeline and return its status; `speech/changed` follows.
- `speech/status` — Return the local pipeline's status plist.
- `speech/stop` — Stop the local pipeline and return its status; `speech/changed` follows.
- `speech/synthesize` (text &optional voice) — Speak TEXT and return a promise of (:audio BASE64 :mime "audio/wav").
- `speech/transcribe` (audio &optional format language) — Transcribe AUDIO, a base64 WAV, and return a promise of (:text TEXT).

### Events

- `speech/changed` — The local speech pipeline's state moved; the argument is its status plist.

### Commands

- `harness-speech-local-start` — Start the local pipeline; CALLBACK gets its status plist.
- `harness-speech-local-stop` — Stop the local pipeline; CALLBACK gets its status plist.

### Options

- `harness-speech-autostart` — Non-nil starts the local pipeline with the harness.
- `harness-speech-local-whisper` — The whisper.cpp model file the bundled stack transcribes with.
- `harness-speech-local-startup-timeout` — Seconds a started pipeline gets to answer before it reads as failed.
- `harness-speech-local-stt-command` — Command the harness runs for speech to text, or nil for its stack.
- `harness-speech-local-stt-url` — URL the speech-to-text command serves, or nil for the stack.
- `harness-speech-local-tts-command` — Command the harness runs for text to speech, or nil for its stack.
- `harness-speech-local-tts-url` — URL the text-to-speech command serves, or nil for the stack.
- `harness-speech-local-voice` — The voice the local pipeline speaks with.
- `harness-speech-request-timeout` — Seconds one transcription or synthesis request may take.

## Uses

### Events it emits

- `speech/changed`

### Hooks it adds to

- `kill-emacs-hook` → `harness-speech--stop-all`
